issues.title: Literal keyword matching **kwargs parameter is expanded twice and can overwrite named arguments
issues.body:
Consumer: uibcdf/pharmacophoremt#6/#82, source 6dc3da62a5d4623b6c22617b8d528582a52b1f79. Reproduced on Python 3.14.7 with published ArgDigest 0.17.0, source c7128f09b2fe064b6c5603d1077dbd2cec52223d; Conda SHA-256 9c35fa297b5a85dc65ac49ccd108f60f08dbeac4f745d6c369a767c0a0b3a3e1. Current read-only sibling cd9c4f3ab80e892075fc5bee9b4ae9ce0ab5e018 has the same relevant implementation.

```python
from argdigest import arg_digest, DigestConfig

@arg_digest(config=DigestConfig(argument_digestion=False, standardizer=None))
def delegate(file_name, **kwargs):
    return file_name, kwargs

marker = object()
assert delegate('original', kwargs=marker) == ('original', {'kwargs': marker})
assert delegate('original', kwargs={'file_name': 'changed'}) == (
    'original', {'kwargs': {'file_name': 'changed'}}
)
```

Actual first result is ('original', {}); actual second is ('changed', {}). A nested {'selection': marker} also becomes a top-level selection instead of retaining the literal kwargs option. Ordinary selection and literal skip_digestion=True contrast controls preserve the examples.

Source: core.utils.bind_arguments already flattens the VAR_KEYWORD container. core.decorator._run_digestion checks for plan.var_keyword_name in the already-flat map and expands/removes it a second time. A caller can legally supply a literal keyword with that name. This occurs before normalization/domain admission and can replace explicit named arguments without a collision refusal.

Current consumer effect: phmt.model(original_source, method='reference-ligand', kwargs={'molecular_system': replacement_source}) reaches a recorded endpoint with replacement_source. An endpoint spy verifies routing only, with no molecular inspection or fabricated chemical answer. Independent candidate and current-consumer probes retain recorded source/native/test/input/metadata identity.

Please preserve literal keyword names/value identity, including a key equal to the VAR_KEYWORD parameter name; apply ordinary domain refusal to unknown keywords without dropping/expanding them. Protect alternate VAR_KEYWORD names, opaque/mapping values, named-argument collisions, aliases/domains, call shape and bypass parity. Generic binding belongs in ArgDigest; no downstream local binding engine/renaming/monkey-patch is proposed. Native I/O migration is deferred until a supported published correction is received. Other consumers may be affected; please assess suite impact before rollout.

issues.title: Support TypeError-compatible contract refusals when adopting existing Python I/O APIs
issues.body:
Consumer: uibcdf/pharmacophoremt#6/#82 at 6dc3da62a5d4623b6c22617b8d528582a52b1f79. Native JSON/YAML readers and writers have closed Python signatures: unsupported keywords raise TypeError before file/model work. Receiving definition-owned contracts must preserve that catch family.

```python
from argdigest import arg_digest, DigestConfig

def original(file_name):
    return file_name

wrapped = arg_digest(config=DigestConfig(argument_digestion=False))(original)
for function in (original, wrapped):
    try:
        function('file.json', typo=True)
    except Exception as error:
        print(type(error).__name__, isinstance(error, TypeError))
# TypeError True
# UnknownArgumentError False
```

Published 0.17.0 changes unknown-keyword and skip_digestion=False refusal to UnknownArgumentError outside TypeError; literal True reaches the original closed callable and retains native TypeError. We measure eight family changes across twelve calls to four real native endpoints. Calls remain refused: this is a compatibility capability request, distinct from the literal-VAR_KEYWORD defect.

Please define a supported provider-owned route to preserve TypeError compatibility for call-shape refusals while retaining ArgDigest code/context and domain enforcement. Opt-in policy, compatible inheritance or provider-owned exception selection are possible designs for the provider to decide. Warn/ignore must not silently discard options. No downstream error/validation engine or undocumented skip configuration is proposed.

Python 3.14.7/public ArgDigest 0.17.0, Conda SHA-256 9c35fa297b5a85dc65ac49ccd108f60f08dbeac4f745d6c369a767c0a0b3a3e1; source/runtime/native identities are retained. Existing PHMT-E108/ValueError schema and PHMT-E109/TypeError filename contracts, native path support and original MolSysMT/provider errors must also remain. Source correction, supported API and installed/public consumer qualification remain separate gates.
